description: Gumbel distribution cumulative distribution function exp(-exp(-(x - mu) / beta)) (location mu, scale beta)

tolerance.reason: x, mu and beta are exact doubles, beta is a power of two and x - mu = beta z with z a double, so z = (x - mu) / beta is exact. F = exp(-w) with w = exp(-z) has condition number w in w, at most 708.4 at a normal result, so rounding w once costs up to 7.9e-14 there (as for weibull_sf), and the outer exp adds an ulp. This assumes an exp within about half an ulp (as glibc's is); one good only to 1 ulp could lose about 1.5e-13 at the grid's worst point (w = 665), which would not by itself be a bug. 1e-13 as for the other functions; results below 2.2e-308 are judged relative to that number (conventions)

grid: (mu, beta) in {(0, 1), (0, 2^-500), (0, 2^500), (-10, 1/4), (100, 8), (-2^1023, 2^1023)} x x = mu + beta z for z = -7..40 step 1/4, z in {-1000, -100, -20, -10, -8, -7.5, 50, 100, 200, 500, 700, 708, 708.5, 709, 710, 720, 740, 745, 746, 800, 1000, 1e5, 1e10, 1e100, 1e300} and z = +-2^-30, kept where x is an exact, finite double that is 0 or normal (so z = (x - mu) / beta is exact); F is subnormal from about z = -6.56, 0 below about z = -6.61 and rounds to 1 above about z = 36.7
